title: Termite Mound Ventilation Airflow Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a Three.js simulation of termite mound ventilation airflow. Load the 'Corset.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/) and use it as the termite mound structure placed at the center of the scene.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 8, 18) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 15, 10) with intensity 0.8.
- A ground plane (50x50) with a brown/earth-toned material.
- Scale the loaded Corset.glb model to roughly 5 units tall and position it at (0, 0, 0). This represents the termite mound.
- Create a translucent cross-section overlay (a vertical plane slicing through the mound center, toggled via UI) to visualize internal airflow channels.

PARTICLE AIRFLOW SYSTEM:
- Implement a particle system representing air molecules flowing through and around the mound.
- Use 500 particles total, each a small sphere (radius 0.05) or point sprite.
- Particles are divided into two categories: 'warm' (rising, colored orange-red) and 'cool' (descending, colored blue-cyan).
- Warm particles spawn near the mound base interior (y near 0, within radius 1.5 of center) and rise upward through the mound with slight turbulence (random x/z perturbation).
- Cool particles spawn at the top of the mound (y near 5) and descend along the outer surface.
- Each particle has velocity (vx, vy, vz). Warm particles have base vy of +1.5 to +3.0. Cool particles have base vy of -1.0 to -2.0.
- When particles exit bounds (y > 7 or y < -1 or distance from center > 8), they respawn at their origin zone.
- Apply a wind factor that can be adjusted, affecting horizontal drift of all particles.

PHYSICS & THERMODYNAMICS:
- Track total thermal energy as the sum of all warm particle speeds multiplied by a constant (0.1 per unit speed).
- Track a mound internal temperature value (starts at 35°C). When simulation speed increases, temperature rises by 0.5°C per speed increment. When speed decreases, temperature drops by 0.5°C.
- Airflow rate = average vy of all warm particles. This value should update each frame.
- Conservation: total particle count must always equal 500 (warm + cool).

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Keyboard 'W': Increase wind strength by 0.5 (max 5.0). Wind adds horizontal vx to all particles.
- Keyboard 'S': Decrease wind strength by 0.5 (min 0.0).
- Keyboard 'ArrowUp': Increase simulation speed multiplier by 0.25 (max 3.0, starts at 1.0).
- Keyboard 'ArrowDown': Decrease simulation speed multiplier by 0.25 (min 0.25).
- Keyboard 'T': Toggle cross-section view (show/hide the translucent slice plane).
- Keyboard 'C': Toggle particle color mode between 'temperature' (warm=red, cool=blue) and 'velocity' (fast=white, slow=green).
- A DOM button with id='btn-reset' that resets simulation to initial state (wind=0, speed=1.0, temp=35, respawn all particles).
- A DOM button with id='btn-toggle-warm' that toggles visibility of warm particles.
- A DOM button with id='btn-toggle-cool' that toggles visibility of cool particles.

HUD / UI:
- A HUD overlay (top-left) showing: Wind Strength, Sim Speed, Mound Temp (°C), Airflow Rate, Warm Count, Cool Count.
- Style with semi-transparent dark background, white text, monospace font.
- Buttons placed at top-right with clear labels.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
  - modelLoaded: boolean (true once Corset.glb is loaded)
  - particleCount: total number of active particles (should always be 500)
  - warmCount: number of warm particles currently active
  - coolCount: number of cool particles currently active
  - windStrength: current wind value (0.0 to 5.0)
  - simSpeed: current simulation speed multiplier (0.25 to 3.0)
  - moundTemp: current mound temperature in °C
  - airflowRate: average vy of warm particles (number)
  - crossSectionVisible: boolean
  - colorMode: 'temperature' or 'velocity'
  - warmVisible: boolean
  - coolVisible: boolean
  - thermalEnergy: total thermal energy (sum of warm particle speeds * 0.1)
  - frameCount: number of animation frames elapsed
  - particlesHaveNaN: boolean (true if any particle has NaN position or velocity)
  - avgWarmVy: average vy of warm particles
  - avgCoolVy: average vy of cool particles
physics_constraints: Warm air rises (positive vy), cool air descends (negative vy). Total particle count conserved at 500. Wind affects horizontal drift proportionally. Thermal energy = sum(warm_speed * 0.1). No NaN values in any particle position or velocity. Mound temperature changes with simulation speed adjustments. Airflow rate correlates with simulation speed multiplier.
